clinicalPearls: This is a chromatin-related overgrowth syndrome characterised by macrocephaly, tall stature, and neurodevelopmental difficulties
It is caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SETD2, a histone methyltransferase gene responsible for trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 36
Intellectual disability, autism spectrum features, and speech and language delay are prominent
Obesity and advanced bone age may accompany the tall stature and macrocephaly
It sits within the differential of Sotos and related overgrowth syndromes and is usually distinguished by molecular testing rather than clinical features alone
Diagnosis is established by exome or genome sequencing, or a targeted overgrowth/intellectual disability panel
Management is supportive and anticipatory, focusing on developmental, educational, and behavioural interventions with surveillance of growth and associated features
reference.pathophysiology: Luscan-Lumish syndrome is an overgrowth disorder within the group of chromatin-modification syndromes. It results from germline heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SETD2, which encodes a histone methyltransferase that catalyses trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 36, an epigenetic mark that regulates transcription, splicing, and DNA repair. Reduced SETD2 activity disturbs these chromatin-dependent gene-expression programmes during development, giving rise to generalised overgrowth, macrocephaly, and neurodevelopmental impairment. Inheritance is autosomal dominant, and reported cases are frequently de novo. As with other genes in this pathway, distinct classes of SETD2 variant have been linked to different clinical presentations.
additionalInvestigations: Exome or genome sequencing, or a targeted overgrowth/intellectual disability gene panel
Chromosomal microarray to exclude copy number causes
Growth monitoring including consideration of bone age
MRI of the brain if neurological signs or marked macrocephaly are present
Ophthalmological and general paediatric review as indicated
redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference or focal neurological signs
Severe behavioural disturbance affecting safety or function
Emergence of features suggesting an alternative or additional diagnosis
reference.prognosis: The condition is not known to shorten lifespan for most individuals, and the outlook is governed principally by the severity of intellectual disability and autism spectrum features. Early and sustained developmental and educational support optimises functional outcomes.
pitfalls: Anchoring on a clinical diagnosis of Sotos syndrome and not extending genetic testing to SETD2
Assuming overgrowth syndromes are clinically distinguishable when molecular testing is usually required
Underestimating the autism spectrum and language needs that benefit from targeted intervention
Omitting genetic counselling regarding autosomal dominant, commonly de novo, inheritance
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: No disease-specific drug therapy; care centres on early developmental and educational intervention for intellectual disability and speech and language delay
Autism-focused behavioural therapy alongside speech, occupational and physiotherapy support
Serial growth monitoring including bone age, with dietetic input to address obesity and overgrowth
Neurological assessment and brain MRI where macrocephaly is marked or neurological signs emerge
Routine ophthalmological and general paediatric surveillance
Coordinate care through a multidisciplinary paediatric and clinical genetics team
Genetic counselling for the autosomal dominant inheritance, with parental testing given the frequency of de novo variants
